courses.subject: P A
courses.title: Foundations of Public Affairs
courses.description: Explore key concepts and debates in the study of public policy. Review foundational historical texts, influential theoretical writings, and important case studies. Discover a range of policy issues, both domestic and international. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Offered on the letter-grade basis only.
courses.offering: Offered on the letter-grade basis only.

courses.subject: P A
courses.title: Analysis of Policy Adoption and Implementation
courses.description: Examine how US policymakers and staff in local, state, and federal government formulate and manage public policy, including the processes for creating and adopting public policy and the processes for implementing and governing public policy. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Offered on the letter-grade basis only.
courses.offering: Offered on the letter-grade basis only.

courses.subject: P A
courses.title: Qualitative Methods for Public Affairs
courses.description: Survey a variety of qualitative empirical methods, drawn from the fields of history, anthropology, political science, and sociology, that are essential for making and evaluating public policies and programs. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Offered on the letter-grade basis only.
courses.offering: Offered on the letter-grade basis only.

courses.subject: P A
courses.title: Quantitative Methods for Public Affairs
courses.description: Survey a variety of quantitative empirical methods, drawn from the fields of data science and management science, that are essential for making and evaluating public policies and programs. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Offered on the letter-grade basis only. Prerequisite: Statistics and Data Sciences 320E with a grade of at least C-.
courses.prereqText: Statistics and Data Sciences 320E with a grade of at least C-.
courses.offering: Offered on the letter-grade basis only.

courses.subject: P A
courses.title: Economic Analysis for Public Affairs
courses.description: Use the tools of microeconomics to analyze the public policymaking role of governments. Examine rationales for policy interventions including addressing market failures, distributional goals, generating revenue, among other objectives. Explore specific policy interventions and topics relevant to contemporary public policy debates such as taxation, health, social welfare, energy and the environment, and income inequality. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Offered on the letter-grade basis only. Prerequisite: Grade of at least C- in Economics 304K.
courses.prereqText: Grade of at least C- in Economics 304K.
courses.offering: Offered on the letter-grade basis only.

courses.description: Restricted to Public Affairs majors. Practice entering the professional realm of policymaking through a series of workshops that focus on different aspects of professional development such as resume-writing, mock job interviews, drafting cover letters for jobs and internships, and professional networking. One lecture hour a week for one semester. Offered on the letter-grade basis only. Prerequisite: Grade of at least C- in Public Affairs 320.

courses.description: Restricted to Public Affairs majors. Discover the basic skills of effective public and nonprofit leadership that promote well-being and strengthen civil society. Determine the characteristics of good leaders, including personal and social responsibility, inclusivity, and ethics. Develop and refine a guiding personal philosophy of leadership for navigating real world applications to advance social and policy change. One lecture hour a week for one semester. Offered on the letter-grade basis only. Prerequisite: Grade of at least C- in Public Affairs 320.
